narrative:
On November 23, 2026, the Karnataka High Court registered an overall hearing rate of 38.4%, taking up 1,118 of the 2,912 scheduled matters across 48 judges. This performance reflects a moderate decline from the 42.8% recorded on November 16 (1,224 of 2,859 matters heard), but an improvement over the 36.0% clearance observed on November 12.

Hearing stage conversions showed substantial variance across procedural categories. Preliminary hearings recorded the strongest efficiency among major stages, converting 54.7% (211 of 386 matters). The orders stage formed the bulk of the docket, clearing 438 of 1,003 scheduled cases (43.7%), a slight decrease from 45.4% on November 16. Admission matters converted at 32.9% (245 of 744), dropping ten percentage points compared to the previous week's 43.0%. Final hearings converted 24.5% (104 of 424), remaining higher than the 14.8% recorded on November 12, whereas further hearings lagged significantly at 11.9% (24 of 201).

Case type distribution was heavily centered on Writ Petitions (WP), which accounted for 1,448 scheduled cases but converted only 32.9% (477 heard), down from 46.3% on November 16. In contrast, Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) achieved a 54.2% hearing rate (150 of 277), outpacing historical marks from November 16 (44.6%) and November 12 (39.4%). Criminal Appeals (CRL.A) also demonstrated strong movement at 61.4% (89 of 145 heard), while Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) converted 36.2% (174 of 481).

Individual judicial output varied widely across court halls. High disposal efficiencies were delivered by B. Pramod (80.4%, 41 of 51 heard), R. Devdas and T.P. Vivekananda (78.7%, 48 of 61), and Shivashankar Amarannavar (68.7% across 131 total scheduled matters). Conversely, severe scheduling congestion led to low conversions in certain halls, including Suraj Govindaraj hearing none of 162 scheduled cases and a 108-case cause list under the Chief Justice bench converting just 7.4%.
